memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses then said to Aaron and his sons, 'Cook the meat at the entrance to the tent of meeting and eat it there with the bread from the basket of ordination offerings, as I commanded, saying, "Aaron and his sons are to eat it." Then burn up the rest of the meat and the bread.'" - Lev 8:31-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The ordination ends with a meal.

After the washing, the robing, the anointing, the blood on ear and hand and foot — Aaron and his sons sit down and eat, at the entrance of the tent, in God's presence.

God's callings do not end in exhaustion. They end at a table.

We often think of consecration as the beginning of hard work, and it is. But before a single day of service, God fed them. Their strength for the ministry came from a meal He provided, eaten in His presence.

Elijah, collapsed under a broom tree and asking to die, was not first given a rebuke or a task. An angel woke him twice and gave him food, and said, The journey is too much for you (1 Kgs 19:7). Ministry came later.

Jesus fed His disciples on a beach after the resurrection before He restored Peter to his calling (Jn 21:12-17).

If you are serving God from a place of depletion, the pattern of Scripture is not to try harder. It is to come and eat. Jesus said, I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry (Jn 6:35).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I serving God out of fullness or out of depletion?
2. When did I last simply receive from God rather than working for Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, feed me before You send me. I come to Your table today needing strength I do not have. Amen.
